one_liner: Single-header C++17/20/23 thread pool that reuses worker threads to avoid std::thread's per-task creation overhead.
what_it_does: BS::thread_pool is a single-header C++ thread pool: submit callables with submit_task() (returns std::future), detach_task() (fire-and-forget), or submit_loop()/detach_loop() for automatic loop parallelization, all run on a fixed set of worker threads created once (default size = hardware_concurrency()). Optional bitmask template features add task priority, pause/resume, and wait-deadlock detection, kept opt-in so the default path stays minimal. It also ships a BS::synced_stream utility for interleaving-free multithreaded console output. It is not a drop-in for std::thread/std::async: you submit work to a shared pool object rather than constructing a thread per call.
how_it_is_fast: The entire speed case is avoiding OS thread creation/teardown per task: threads are spawned once at pool construction and repeatedly pull work off one shared task queue guarded by a mutex/condition variable for the pool's lifetime, instead of std::thread's per-call CreateThread()/clone(). Optional features (priority, pause, deadlock checks) are selected via a bitmask template parameter, so pools that don't enable them pay no extra runtime cost. There is no work-stealing, lock-free queue, or SIMD involved -- it is one shared FIFO queue plus thread reuse, not algorithmic scheduling cleverness.
when_to_use: Need a zero-dependency, header-only pool that drops into an existing C++17 project without a new build dependency
Many short-lived tasks (thousands+) where std::thread's per-call OS thread creation would dominate runtime
Want built-in loop parallelization (submit_loop/detach_loop) instead of hand-rolling chunking over std::thread
Need optional task priority, pause/resume, or deadlock detection without adopting a larger framework like oneTBB or Taskflow
HPC/scientific-computing workloads with many uniform-sized tasks, where a single shared queue is enough
when_not_to_use: Imbalanced task graphs where some threads finish early and idle -- no work-stealing, so tail latency suffers vs. TooManyCooks/dispenso/libfork under uneven task sizes
Need a hard measured number vs. std::thread/std::async before adopting -- none is published; only a self-referential single-vs-multithreaded Mandelbrot speedup is measured
Calling wait()/wait_for()/wait_until() recursively from inside a task on the same pool without enabling wait_deadlock_checks -- deadlocks silently by default (documented in the README's own example)
Need fiber/coroutine-style cooperative scheduling or tight oneTBB/OpenMP interop -- this is a plain OS-thread pool
Apple Clang + C++20 module import path: README states Apple Clang is not officially supported there (plain header-only include is unaffected)

integration.min_toolchain: C++17 (C++20/23 optional, enables module import and extra perf); verified with Clang 21, GCC 15, MSVC 19.50
integration.platforms: any C++17-conformant compiler/OS; native extensions (thread/process priority, affinity, naming) additionally target Windows, Linux, macOS
integration.thread_safety: not documented as a blanket guarantee -- task submission (submit_task/detach_task/etc.) and reset() are described as safe to call at any time, but no formal per-function thread-safety table is given
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial -- replaces manual std::thread construction with a shared pool object and a submit/detach API; call sites must change, it is not a constructor-signature swap

gotchas: wait()/wait_for()/wait_until() called from inside a task running on the same pool deadlocks by default; opting into BS::tp::wait_deadlock_checks (BS::wdc_thread_pool) turns that into a thrown BS::wait_deadlock instead of a hang

Optional features (priority, pause, wait-deadlock checks) are chosen via a bitmask template parameter at the pool's type, so combining features means a distinct pool type per combination, not a runtime toggle
The pool cannot forcibly terminate a running task; cancellation requires the task itself to poll a flag
Task priority is a signed 8-bit value (-128 to 127, higher runs first) only when BS::tp::priority is enabled -- ignored otherwise
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick BS::thread_pool over Boost.Fiber, dispenso, TooManyCooks, libfork, or Taskflow when you want one self-contained header with zero dependencies beyond the standard library and don't need work-stealing or fiber-level concurrency; pick a work-stealing pool instead (dispenso, TooManyCooks, libfork) when task sizes are uneven or you need a published std::thread/std::async number, which this project doesn't provide.
verified_claims_summary: No direct std::thread- or std::async-vs-pool number is published anywhere in the README; the only measured figure is a 24.2x multithreaded-vs-single-threaded speedup on the project's own Mandelbrot benchmark (32-thread Intel i9-13900K, MSVC, C++23, /O2), which quantifies parallel scaling of the pool itself, not the per-task OS-thread-creation overhead the Motivation section claims std::thread has.
status_note: Actively maintained (pushed 2026-01-04, 0 open issues, MIT-licensed, 3,055 stars, companion SoftwareX paper and arXiv:2105.00613); single header is trivially small enough to vendor into any project.
